clue.text: Previous examination of a clergyman

parts.note: previous means bygone, past
a viva or spoken test is an oral

explanation.surface: A clergyman's earlier test is being recalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral work is the care a priest gives a congregation, so the adjective describes a clergyman's role.

clue.text: Hand it down to Daddy's boy

parts.note: Daddy is pa, so Daddy's is pa's
a boy is a son

explanation.surface: An heirloom is handed down to a father's son.
explanation.definitionFit: To bequeath something to the next generation is to transmit it onwards.

clue.text: Couple inhabiting place find a water nymph

indicators.note: inhabiting means living inside, so the couple goes within the place

parts.note: a site is a place
pr is the abbreviation for pair, a couple

explanation.surface: A couple living somewhere discover a water nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf or fairy, and in older use a spirit of water or air.

clue.text: Work in a point to declare one's views

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
taken as written
E for east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Fit a point into a piece of work to express an opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but simply supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an opinion or state what one thinks is to express a view.

clue.text: One shade that needs paint solvent

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A single colour needs a solvent for paint.
explanation.definitionFit: This volatile liquid dissolves paint and nail varnish, a common thinner.

clue.text: A hundred in a coach. You can count on it

indicators.note: in tells us the first pair of pieces is placed inside the other

parts.note: a coach is a bus, so 'a coach' gives A BUS
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred people squeeze into a coach, and you can rely on it.
explanation.walkthrough: AC goes inside A BUS, after its B. 'You can count on it' is a cheeky definition: a frame of beads is literally counted on.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead frame is a calculating device, the thing one literally counts on.

clue.text: Trifle with beautiful woman concealing a gun

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the woman holds the other pieces

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Toying with a beauty who has a gun hidden on her.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is something trivial, an unimportant thing.

clue.text: Manage to make tin cover

indicators.note: the letters are used to make a new word

explanation.surface: Managing to produce a lid for a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed in bringing something about despite difficulty is to manage it.

clue.text: Flag which is generally recognised

explanation.surface: A flag that everyone knows.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a military banner and something normal or customary.

clue.text: Used a colander when under stress

definitions.meaning: passing food through a sieve to drain it

explanation.definitionFit: Draining liquid through a sieve is to sieve it, and stretched nerves or relations are tense: two senses of one verb form.

clue.text: Muslim ruler about to conclude committee business

indicators.note: about means going round, so the ruler's title is placed around the next piece

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman or Muslim commander or chief
to conclude is to end

explanation.surface: A Muslim ruler is on the point of closing a committee's business.
explanation.definitionFit: The list of items a committee must deal with at a meeting is its schedule of business.

clue.text: Man has a piano, but it's a wreck

parts.note: he is a male person
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A man owns a piano that is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' means softly in music, abbreviated P, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilapidated old car or building is informally called a wreck.

clue.text: He told one to become unemployed

indicators.note: the words are made to become something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone was told by a man that they had lost their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on state benefit for the jobless is a British idiom for being out of work; the dole is unemployment pay.

clue.text: The German takes it back when exhausted

indicators.note: back means the whole run of letters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: der is German for 'the'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A German takes something back when he is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the German article together with the pronoun as one run; 'takes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worn out and weary is fatigued, the same as drained.

clue.text: Fruit providing calcium

definitions.meaning: quicklime, calcium oxide, a white caustic substance

explanation.surface: A fruit that gives you calcium.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a green citrus fruit and the calcium oxide made by burning limestone.

clue.text: Bound to mature after being kept for duty

indicators.note: after places the maturing piece behind the duty piece

parts.note: goods held in bond are stored by customs until duty is paid
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Wine destined to mature while kept in bond until duty is paid.
explanation.walkthrough: Goods 'in bond' sit in a customs warehouse until the duty is paid, which is why the surface sounds like wine-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tied up, enslaved, or held captive is to be bound.

clue.text: Fuss caused by father needing large bowl of water

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a laver is a large basin for washing, as in a temple or church

explanation.surface: Dad makes a fuss about needing a big basin of water.
explanation.walkthrough: LAVER is an old word for a large washing basin, chiefly biblical.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome fuss and bother, needless talk and ado, is the sense of this word.

clue.text: Obscure stratagem adopted by Jack Goodman

indicators.note: the stratagem is taken on by the pieces before it, so it follows them

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)
a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
a ruse is a trick or stratagem

explanation.surface: Jack Goodman uses an obscure trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack Goodman' looks like a person's name, but it splits into a sailor and a saint; 'adopted by' puts the trick after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard to understand is recondite and difficult.

clue.text: Bet tear leads to dramatic scene

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
a tear is a drop

explanation.surface: A lost bet brings tears, a dramatic moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The painted cloth behind a stage set is the scenery behind the action.

clue.text: Friar takes walk to find blackberry

parts.note: a friar is addressed as Brother, abbreviated Br
to amble is to walk slowly

explanation.surface: A friar goes for a stroll to pick blackberries.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly bush that bears blackberries gives its name to the fruit too, especially in Britain.

clue.text: Always sounds like a Bronte heroine

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is pronounced as the word for always

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A Bronte heroine who always sounds the same.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER, poetic for 'ever', is pronounced like 'air'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane, the governess heroine of Charlotte Bronte's novel, has this surname.

clue.text: Charge an old copper to cater for others

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
d was the symbol for a penny, a copper coin, in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Someone charges an old penny for catering for other people.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide food for people is to cater for them.

clue.text: Accessory suiting healthy people to a T

parts.note: fit means in good health
men are people
taken as written

explanation.surface: An accessory that suits fit people perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitment is a fixed fitting, such as a cupboard, an accessory piece of furniture.

clue.text: Cardinal accommodated by cathedral priest is a big gun

indicators.note: accommodated by means housed inside, so the cardinal sits within the priest

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral
N for north is a cardinal point of the compass

explanation.surface: A cardinal staying with a cathedral priest is an important figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it is a cardinal point, N; 'big gun' is a piece of artillery here.
explanation.definitionFit: A large heavy artillery piece is a field gun.

clue.text: Contemptible description of a rubella sufferer

definitions.meaning: rubella is German measles, so a patient is covered in its spots

explanation.definitionFit: The word means miserably small or mean, and jokingly someone covered with measles spots.

clue.text: Suitable inscription for Baker's birthday voucher

parts.note: a birthday cake is inscribed 'To' plus the name of the person it is for
Kenneth Baker was a prominent British Conservative cabinet minister of the 1980s, known as Ken Baker

explanation.surface: What a baker would pipe on a cake for a birthday, as a gift voucher.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cake baker; Baker is the politician Ken Baker, so his birthday cake would read 'TO KEN'.
explanation.definitionFit: A book or gift token is a voucher exchangeable for goods.

clue.text: To settle the score I later returned and dined

indicators.note: returned means these words are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: to dine is to eat, past tense ate

explanation.surface: To get even, I came back later and had dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns I LATER into RETALI, which is followed by ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting back at someone for a wrong done is getting even with them.

clue.text: Member gets nothing for dance

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A member gets nothing in return for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean dance in which one bends back under a low bar is this.

clue.text: A Franco-Spanish coin is not genuine

parts.note: Franco- means French, and un is French for 'a'
the real was an old Spanish silver coin

explanation.surface: A coin from the French-Spanish border is a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imaginary or false is fake, not authentic.

clue.text: End of a semester in America

parts.note: a semester is an academic term
in the US

explanation.surface: The end of a college semester in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stop of a railway or bus line is its end point.

clue.text: Saw telepathy die out

parts.note: ESP stands for extrasensory perception, which includes telepathy

indicators.note: out means the letters of the word die are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone saw their powers of telepathy fading away.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of something is to have seen it, past tense.

clue.text: Counsel a sober French marshal with heart of gold

indicators.note: having gold at its heart means gold is set in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so sober
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Advice for a teetotal French marshal who has a heart of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with heart of gold' puts the heraldic gold in the middle, between the teetotal letters and the marshal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer acting for a client is their counsel, the legal adviser.
